instructions: Put the chicken in a large pot (at least 6 quarts) and cover with cold water to the top of the breast. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming off the foam that rises.

Push the cloves into the onion. Cut the leek and celery into 3 pieces each, halve the carrots and halve the turnips. Add them to the pot with the garlic, peppercorns, thyme, bay leaf and 1 tsp of the salt.

Bring back to a boil, skim once more, then turn the heat to medium low. Cover and simmer gently 2 hours, until the chicken is very tender. That should be about 180°F in the thickest part of the thigh; a thermometer is optional. Without one, the leg should wiggle loose and the juices should run clear.

About 25 minutes before the end, ladle 1 3/4 cups of the hot broth into a saucepan and bring it to a boil. Stir in the rice and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, cover and cook on low 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered 5 minutes.
Lift the chicken onto a plate and let it rest 10 minutes. Taste the broth and add salt and pepper if it needs it. Take out the bay leaf.
Cut or pull the chicken into pieces. Serve it with the vegetables over the rice, with the broth ladled over. Leftover broth keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings was found. Pardon Your French (5.0 from 3 votes) is the lead for the plain poached chicken with root vegetables, with the simmer shortened from 2 1/2 to 2 hours for a smaller bird. The Good Life France cooks the rice in the chicken broth and serves a cream sauce, which is left out; the rice in broth is borrowed. Food Network's Ariane Daguin version is a stuffed capon feast and was not followed. Scaled from 6 servings to 4. The broth is the batch part.
